title: India just laid the foundation for a shipyard that can build 200-metre warships
sources: Maritime Gateway - GRSE & YIL embark on major expansion of shipbuilding and defence manufacturing capabilities in West Bengal
Eastern Mirror Nagaland - Rajnath Singh lays foundation for 5 expansion projects of GRSE, Yantra India
caption:
India just laid the foundation for a shipyard that can build 200-metre warships. Five projects, one state, over Rs 3,400 crore.

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh laid foundation stones for five brownfield expansion projects by GRSE and Yantra India Limited in West Bengal, anchored by a new 32-acre shipbuilding hub at Raichak on the Hooghly. The Raichak hub alone carries over Rs 2,500 crore of investment, with a 200-metre dry dock designed to let GRSE build warships up to 200 metres and commercial vessels up to 60,000 DWT. Three more projects round out the expansion across Shalimar, Kidderpore and the Ishapore Metal and Steel Factory.

One shipyard upgrade is routine maintenance. Five at once, anchored by a hub built for 200-metre ships, is a statement.
